findings.evidence: The accessory name and prescription are visible, but its set fields remain below the fixed footer. Warm-up and main-lift cards each retain a separate section-heading strip and substantial vertical spacing. The prior density objection remains partly unresolved.
findings.userConsequence: Logging the third exercise requires scrolling, and the complete session's entered sets cannot be surveyed in the initial viewport.
findings.suggestedChange: Trim repeated section-header space and card padding enough to expose the accessory set row while preserving the current readable prescription and set text.

findings.evidence: Workout prescriptions, History/More tools, timer actions and notes share a subdued green-gray treatment. Library previews and counts use similarly muted small text. They are readable, but require closer attention than the primary values.
findings.userConsequence: Task-relevant instructions and secondary actions are harder to scan quickly, particularly beside the much brighter set values.
findings.suggestedChange: Strengthen task-relevant secondary foregrounds slightly and distinguish prescription text from optional metadata. Preserve the restrained dark palette.

findings.evidence: The bounded desktop column still places Everyday Strength at the far left and Open plus the overflow menu at the far right of a mostly empty row. Workout tools are now grouped beside their exercise names, but the routine-row separation remains.
findings.userConsequence: Opening a routine requires unnecessary horizontal scanning and pointer travel between its name and action.
findings.suggestedChange: Place Open beside the routine information or give routine rows a narrower internal layout within the stable page frame.

findings.evidence: Movement entries appear as text blocks inside one shared surface, without trailing chevrons or individual row boundaries. The introductory sentence explains that they open, but the rows themselves provide little visual action cue.
findings.userConsequence: A user scanning past the introduction can read the movements as a static report and overlook access to their sessions.
findings.suggestedChange: Add a restrained trailing chevron or another consistent row-level opening affordance, matching Library.

strengths: The copy/paste AI workflow is immediately understandable. Copy prompt, Go to Import, import recovery and export actions have clear priority.
Routine overview names the next workout and week and explicitly separates Plan: Draft from Logged: Done, resolving the prior visible status ambiguity.
Rest editing now has a bordered control and recognizable icon. Bodyweight set notation is consistent across the current workout and exercise history.
Desktop navigation and content alignment are consistent across all four captures. Exercise tools sit beside their names, and the duplicate hamburger is absent.
Onboarding, import resolution and the unfinished builder explain their next actions and consequences clearly.
History sorting states its direction, exercise history supplies volume units, and Profile provides readable dates and explicit bodyweight change.
Library equipment filters use clear text, and category previews provide useful context without overflowing the viewport.
Workspace gives backup clear priority and visibly distinguishes destructive import. The session summary is concise and has an obvious next action.
limitations: Opened every one of the 27 manifest images directly with the image-viewing tool. All were readable.
Read the nine prior reviews, all three prior assessments and the round 03 implementation response. No other current-round output or parent conversation was consulted.
Earlier screenshots were not opened, so no direct image-to-image regression claim is made. Remaining prior objections are identified in the findings; no new major issue was established.
Contrast judgments are visual impressions. No contrast ratios or accessibility conformance were measured.
Static captures cannot establish keyboard behavior, accessible names, touch target bounds, persistence, data safety or scrolling behavior.
Evidence covers 390x844 mobile and 1280x900 desktop viewports, with four dark screens. Workspace appearance controls remain partially below the captured fold.
No source inspection, live interaction, app mutation, file edits, installation, commits, pushes or delegation was performed.
